This is immediately followed by a dramatic close-up of a painting depicting a figure with exaggerated proportions, possibly representing a mythological or allegorical representation of humanity's past suffering. The narration emphasizes the importance of avoiding misconceptions about the "enclosure" (an old term for fencing off common lands) which occurred over 500 years ago in England. This event involved nobles erecting fences around communal farmland, effectively taking control of the land previously used by peasants for farming. The speaker argues that while today's concept of owning property seems natural and straightforward, such practices were not considered normal back then; they represent a radical shift towards private property rights—a notion now seen as deeply rooted in modern capitalism.

The visuals transition between scenes illustrating the past and present. A vivid depiction of a rural village during the medieval period shows people working in fields surrounded by simple wooden structures made of straw roofs—this serves as a backdrop to the discussion. In contrast, later frames feature stylized animations including a cartoonish red devil character wearing headphones, symbolizing skepticism or critique regarding current societal issues. Text overlays appear throughout these images, reinforcing the theme of questioning established norms and highlighting how outdated ideas can be misleading when viewed through contemporary lenses. These elements work together to create a compelling narrative exploring fundamental questions about power dynamics, economic systems, and our evolving relationship with nature and resources.

The narrator then begins explaining that for centuries after this event, people were shocked when British colonists came to America and claimed ownership over land they had never seen before. They asked what was happening if someone owned the land, which made them feel strange about the idea of private property. This concept wasn't common back then; during the early 1600s, European settlers like those living in Manhattan traded goods such as food items worth around $1200 per acre—equivalent to roughly 130,000 won today—for Native American lands. However, because land ownership was not yet considered normal, the indigenous peoples accepted these transactions differently than modern-day practices. Instead of selling the land outright, they agreed to share it equally among themselves. In contrast to how we think of owning real estate now, the earth existed independently—it didn’t belong solely to any one person but rather served all life forms collectively. As the story continues, the speaker wonders aloud whether kings actually held control over land, raising questions about power dynamics within society. A final thought emerges: while humans might have lived off Earth’s resources, there remains ambiguity regarding whose true authority lies above others' lives.

vlm_mm_description: In this thought-provoking video segment, an animated devil-like character wearing headphones delivers a powerful message about the evolution of ownership and control over resources. The scene opens with a red background displaying a poll question: "Why did people choose to own land?" with two options listed—“Don't care” at 67% and “Want to be treated as property” at 33%. This reflects a societal shift toward individualism and private ownership, particularly concerning land use. The narrator explains that while some individuals sought profit through farming, others took advantage of nature for leisure activities such as hunting and fishing, creating new forms of exploitation. These practices involved privatizing shared natural spaces like forests and rivers, leading to what's known as the enclosure movement—a historical phenomenon where common lands were transformed into privately owned properties. Today, similar patterns emerge with artificial intelligence (AI), which operates under the same exploitative logic, allowing corporations and tech giants to monopolize digital space without accountability. The speaker emphasizes how web-based systems have evolved similarly; unlike physical earth, the internet has no inherent ownership rights because it was created by Burner Slay, whose original intent was to share his work freely rather than retain exclusive control. As he continues speaking, the screen transitions to black, highlighting the irony behind these developments—the idea that even our most fundamental tools can become instruments of inequality when they're not properly regulated. Through vivid imagery and symbolic visuals, the narration underscores themes of power dynamics, technological innovation, and the need for ethical governance in both real-world and virtual environments.

vlm_mm_description: In this animated video segment, an orange devil-like character wearing headphones appears against a black background, delivering a commentary about the evolution of the internet and its impact on modern society. The character's expression shifts subtly as it speaks, conveying both curiosity and critical insight. On screen, Korean subtitles appear at the bottom of the frame, translating the speaker’s words: "Why do we believe that making the web freely available provides greater value for people?" This sets up the central theme—how the open-source nature of early internet platforms like the World Wide Web led to massive innovation and growth. As the narration unfolds, the character explains how the birth of the web in 1993 marked the beginning of a new era, leading to rapid expansion across various services such as Yahoo (1994), Google (1998), Facebook (2004), YouTube (2005), and Twitter (2006). These technologies have been described as being relatively young compared to their current age; even though they were developed over three decades ago, many still feel surprisingly fresh. A notable point made during the discussion is the comparison between past and present digital ecosystems—the concept of “the second enclosure” referenced by Duke University Law School professor James Boyle, highlighting how today’s online world mirrors historical patterns of monopolistic control through data ownership. The narrator emphasizes that just as land was once considered unowned under previous models, so too has access to information now become controlled by private entities operating within vast networks. By drawing parallels between these two eras, the video aims to provoke reflection on whether our current digital landscape continues the same trend toward centralized power and limited openness.

vlm_mm_description: The scene begins with a red background displaying two parallel diagrams that compare the historical structure of land ownership (inland) with the modern digital economy (web). The top diagram shows Earth as an agricultural landmass controlled by "regents" who manage the land for profit; this is likened to how past feudal lords managed farmland. The bottom diagram illustrates the web as a digital landscape owned by corporations like Google, Facebook, and YouTube—these companies operate within a system similar to the old model but now run through digital platforms. A cartoon devil character wearing headphones appears at the lower right corner, reacting thoughtfully while listening to the speaker's narration. As the narrator explains, both systems have evolved: people once worked hard cultivating land under landlords' control, producing goods and services which were then sold back to them. In contrast, today’s internet ecosystem allows users to create art, music, videos, etc., using shared resources such as servers and bandwidth provided by tech giants. These creators benefit financially when others use these tools, leading to increased user engagement and revenue generation for businesses. This creates a symbiotic relationship between corporate entities and creative individuals, much like the traditional agrarian society where farmers supported themselves through labor-intensive farming practices. However, despite similarities in economic models, there remains significant divergence due to technological advancements and shifts in power dynamics. Specifically, the core issue highlighted by the speaker relates to the fundamental shift in ownership rights—the idea that those who created something valuable should retain control over it rather than allowing free access without compensation. Ultimately, the discussion centers around whether current structures reflect true equality or perpetuate existing inequalities rooted in unequal distribution of wealth across generations.

vlm_mm_description: A red cartoon devil character wearing headphones stands against a black background, speaking with an intense expression as he discusses the concept of "Inclusion" (잉클로저) and how artificial intelligence has evolved since its inception. The screen displays Korean text that reads "내 쫓는거거든요 같이 쓰었던 땅에 욜타리를 치고여긴 내 거야 있 dang 내 거니까 너네 는 나가 했 던 게 인클로저핵심인데 지금까지 제가 말씀한 말을 들으면어때요?" which translates roughly to: "I'm chasing you guys... I've fenced off my land together; this is mine now! It's not about going out but coming in—everyone come here and create together, share money and resources like us!" He continues explaining that while Inclusion was previously similar to what existed before, the current state of AI development began right now, when ideas such as Google's Gemini, Microsoft's Group, OpenAI's ChatGPT, and Entropic Cloud emerged. These models are developed by tech companies, yet they don't eat food or grow up through natural processes—they rely entirely on human-created data. The speaker questions whether these systems truly consume anything meaningful, emphasizing that people must be involved in creating material for them to function properly. As he speaks, the visuals shift to show a sheep standing next to the devil figure, symbolizing the source of nourishment for these AI entities—the very creations humans make. Text overlays appear reading “네 거 먹금” (“That’s what we’re eating”), highlighting the core issue at hand: the dependency of advanced AI technologies on human-generated content rather than self-sustaining growth mechanisms. This creates a critical reflection on ownership, creation, and intellectual property within digital ecosystems.

vlm_mm_description:
In this video clip, a narrator expresses profound concern about the current state of technology and copyright, highlighting how artificial intelligence (AI) development has become an issue involving human creators and large corporations. The speaker begins by stating that "strange times" have arrived, noting that companies like B.O.3 have achieved great success due to being built using YouTube content, which were then used as raw data for machine learning models. This practice—where user-generated videos are taken directly and used without permission—is described as unethical and potentially illegal, especially since such content often lacks proper licensing agreements. The narration emphasizes that while these platforms claim to be open-source, there’s no clear evidence of ownership rights being respected; instead, users’ work becomes part of corporate datasets, raising serious questions about intellectual property theft.

The screen transitions to show three prominent AI tools: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude. Each tool is represented visually with distinct icons and stylized figures. The narrator suggests that despite having similar capabilities, these systems differ significantly in terms of design philosophy and ethical standards. They point out that although some might argue that these services are essentially copying one another, the core difference lies in their underlying principles and values. For instance, the use of copyrighted material within training sets raises concerns about fairness and transparency across industries.

Next, the focus shifts to Claude, introduced as a new company whose rise reflects broader changes in digital innovation. According to the subtitles, Claude gained significant attention because it refused to sign contracts with Trump administration officials, citing safety issues related to potential misuse of its platform. As a result, the company faced unprecedented national-level retaliation but managed to gain public support through positive reception. Its application reached number-one rankings in major mobile applications such as iOS and Android store categories, demonstrating strong market appeal even amid political controversy.

Finally, the video concludes with humorous imagery depicting Donald Trump pointing at two other characters labeled “Kak” and “Aa,” representing opposing views—one seemingly supportive of technological advancement while the other opposes it. These visuals underscore the complex relationship between politics, ethics, and emerging technologies. Overall, the sequence presents a critical examination of modern tech trends, particularly focusing on how creative expression intersects with commercial interests and global governance structures.

A surreal animation then appears—a red devil-like figure wearing headphones—symbolizing the growing fear among people regarding the potential consequences of unchecked technological advancement. vlm_mm_description: A red screen displays an article headline about tech companies arguing they made "fair use" of copyrighted materials to develop innovative technology like ChatGPT, suggesting this practice might be harming the rapidly growing AI industry. A cartoon devil-like figure wearing headphones appears on the right side of the screen, reacting to the discussion. The narrator expresses concern over how paying royalties to copyright holders could stifle innovation, comparing the situation to a "hamstringing" (발목을 잡다) of the AI industry. They then ask if there was a similar legal provision in history called the "Merton Statute" which gave landowners rights to manage shared lands, but only under certain conditions—specifically, leaving enough grazing space for tenant farmers. This condition was vague and open to interpretation, leading to disputes among landlords and eventually becoming a precedent for modern digital sharing practices. In contrast, today’s technological innovations rely heavily on complex laws regarding "Fair Use", whose four criteria include the intended use, the nature of the original work, the extent of usage relative to the entire work, and the impact on the market value of the original piece. These elements remain ambiguous, creating uncertainty around what constitutes legitimate use. The speaker notes that while these rules exist, they lack clarity and can lead to confusion, especially since many people believe they're making ethical choices through creative reuse. As the narration continues, the focus shifts to explaining the actual components of the Fair Use doctrine according to Article 107 of the Copyright Law, emphasizing that determining whether something qualifies requires careful evaluation across all four factors mentioned above. The final part highlights how even though some aspects seem reasonable, others still leave room for debate due to unclear boundaries between personal creativity and public access.

This discussion emphasizes that while some argue this constitutes transformative use—where data is learned and new results created—the courts remain divided, especially regarding the impact on markets. vlm_mm_description: In this animated video segment set in the year 2026, an ominous red devil-like character wearing headphones appears against a stark white background, symbolizing the looming challenges of artificial intelligence (AI) lawsuits. The narrator begins by highlighting that in the United States alone, over 50 copyright infringement cases have been filed against AI companies so far in 2026—marking a significant escalation in legal battles between human creators and emerging technology firms. As summer approaches, viewers are informed that definitive rulings regarding fair use will soon be issued, potentially reshaping how laws treat digital innovation and intellectual property rights. This development holds profound implications for society as we navigate the future of creativity and ownership under increasingly complex technological landscapes. To underscore these concerns, the speaker draws parallels to historical developments concerning landownership and power structures during the early modern period. Specifically, they reference the evolution of "inclusivity" — a term used here metaphorically to describe the shift from small-scale private landholding practices supported by aristocratic elites to larger-scale monopolies driven by institutionalized control. In England’s political system at the time, when King Charles I attempted to curb such encroachments through legislation, he failed due to entrenched opposition led not only by his own court but also by powerful members of Parliament who were themselves tied closely to traditional landed nobility. These figures had long held sway over agricultural lands and economic resources, making them formidable opponents even before the rise of centralized state authority. By connecting contemporary issues about AI litigation with centuries-old patterns of feudalism and legislative resistance, the narration emphasizes the importance of understanding past precedents in order to anticipate current trends. Ultimately, the message conveyed is one of urgency: if today's courts continue favoring corporate interests over public interest, then our very foundation—a balance between individual expression and collective governance—may face irreversible erosion.

vlm_mm_description:
In this animated historical commentary sequence, the story unfolds through a blend of satirical visuals and dramatic narration about the profound impact of land ownership laws on society. The central theme centers around how political power, wielded by aristocratic elites, led to the creation of over four thousand favorable legal statutes that allowed them to legally acquire vast tracts of communal land. This process initiated what became known as the "First Enclosure" period, during which only three percent of shared lands were officially privatized. However, after the law was enacted, the second enclosure phase saw nearly all remaining public land converted into private property, effectively transforming these areas into exclusive real estate holdings. As the landowners accumulated wealth, they began constructing housing developments and eventually established thriving real estate businesses—marking the transition from agrarian economies to modern capitalist ventures. 

The narrative then shifts focus to the irony and injustice embedded within this transformation. It highlights that while ordinary citizens had little influence over such legislation, the technology-driven business leaders—the CEOs of tech companies—were uniquely aware of the importance of these laws. They actively engaged in massive lobbying efforts to ensure that the new legal framework favored their interests, demonstrating an insatiable desire for financial gain at the expense of democratic principles. Their relentless pursuit of legislative change reveals a deeper critique of systemic inequality, suggesting that those who control the means of production also hold disproportionate power over societal structures.

Visually, the scene uses symbolic imagery to underscore this tension. A cartoonish devil figure wearing headphones floats above a sprawling suburban neighborhood, representing the corruptive forces behind the enclosures. Meanwhile, a depiction of George Washington stands beside a stylized column, symbolizing the original ideals of democracy versus the entrenched privilege of the ruling class. In one frame, a man resembling Trump speaks directly to the camera, referencing his opposition to regulations aimed at protecting small farmers—a nod to the broader debate surrounding agricultural policy and economic fairness. vlm_mm_description: In this powerful and somber video sequence, the story unfolds through a series of stark visuals and chilling narration that explore the dark legacy of systemic oppression and industrial transformation. The opening shot presents a close-up of a person wearing a black balaclava, symbolizing resistance and anonymity; the word "Blacks" is prominently displayed over the figure's obscured face, immediately establishing the central theme: racial injustice. This is juxtaposed with an animated graphic showing a red background with the words "BLACK ACT," emphasizing the historical gravity of the subject matter. The narrative then shifts to illustrate how Black people were subjected to brutal laws like the infamous **Black Act**, which was described as one of the most cruel acts in British history—specifically known for its harsh penalties such as death upon minor infractions, including being forced to wear masks or having their faces painted black if they did not conform to societal expectations. These punishments extended beyond mere physical harm, targeting even those without any criminal act committed. For example, anyone caught stealing anything—even just looking at something—could be sentenced to execution. As the camera pans across illustrations depicting animals (deer, rabbit, fish) trapped within enclosures labeled “Enclosed,” viewers witness the metaphorical representation of confinement and exploitation under these oppressive conditions. The accompanying subtitles highlight the absurdity and cruelty of these measures while also pointing out the broader social consequences. Meanwhile, scenes transition to show factories emitting smokestacks, illustrating the economic shift brought about by industrialization—a process that led to significant changes in society but came at great human cost. The final frames depict a cartoonish devil-like character expressing disbelief at the idea that no government has ever been able to stop such atrocities, underscoring the enduring nature of these injustices despite attempts at reform. Overall, the video serves as both a critique of past systems of control and a warning against repeating similar mistakes in modern times.

vlm_mm_description: In this historical drama-style video, a red devil-like character wearing headphones speaks over a montage of scenes depicting the harsh realities of societal oppression during the Industrial Revolution. The story begins with grim imagery showing workers being forced to labor under oppressive conditions, as depicted in a painting that shows people working in factories while others suffer from poverty. This leads to the narrator's explanation about how resistance against tyranny has been repeatedly met with brutal punishment, including executions for those deemed "undesirable" by powerful elites. As the narration continues, we see the rise of the "poor law," which was implemented by the government after previous attempts at social control failed. This new policy involved providing basic necessities such as food, shelter, and money to impoverished individuals, effectively creating a system designed to prevent further unrest. Despite these efforts, the number of homeless and destitute citizens remained high. In contrast to earlier punitive measures, the introduction of the "poor laws" marked a shift towards more humane but still effective governance strategies aimed at stabilizing society. The final segment reveals the connection between past policies and modern concepts like universal basic income (UBI). By drawing parallels between the ancient practice of offering aid to the needy and today’s discussions around UBI, the speaker highlights how both aim to address economic inequality and ensure survival when traditional employment systems fail due to technological advancements and automation. While acknowledging the similarities, the narrator also points out significant differences—such as the fact that current technologies might render human labor obsolete, leading to potential job displacement—and questions whether the original approach would work again in light of evolving challenges posed by artificial intelligence. Overall, the video presents a compelling exploration of history's recurring themes related to class struggle, state intervention, and the quest for equitable living standards across generations.

vlm_mm_description: In this animated discussion segment, a stylized red devil-like character wearing headphones appears against a stark white background, symbolizing skepticism or critical thinking about modern societal issues. The character's expression shifts subtly throughout the clip, reflecting deep concern as they deliver an impassioned critique of Universal Basic Income (UBI). They begin by questioning public perception of basic income, highlighting how AI-driven automation threatens employment across industries—specifically pointing out that even within large corporations like Microsoft, there’s growing unease over the idea of giving people money without any conditions for work. This leads them to argue that while many see UBI as a solution to economic despair caused by job loss due to technology, such policies risk undermining human dignity and creating dependency rather than empowering individuals through innovation. Instead, the speaker advocates for "data sovereignty" — emphasizing that data should be treated as a valuable asset belonging to those who generate it, not merely exploited by corporate entities. Similarly, child labor regulations arose out of similar struggles, highlighting the importance of addressing systemic inequalities rooted in human relationships. vlm_mm_description: The video presents a somber and urgent commentary on the growing crisis of loneliness and isolation among young people in Korea and globally, highlighting how this emotional pain has shifted towards artificial intelligence (AI). The opening frames establish a stark statistic: Korean youth, particularly those aged 19-34, face an alarming increase in social isolation, with the rate rising significantly since two years ago—now reaching levels that suggest nearly every third person feels isolated. This trend is further emphasized by data showing that 75% of isolated individuals have thought about self-isolation but only 26% have actually tried to act on it. The global scale of this issue is also highlighted, with reports indicating that approximately one hundred thousand people per hour feel lonely enough to die—a grim figure underscoring the severity of the problem. As the narration unfolds, the focus shifts to the psychological toll of this isolation, which now seems to be being addressed not through human connection, but via digital companionship. The speaker notes that while humans once sought out friends and family, they are increasingly turning to AI tools like chatbots and virtual assistants, especially during times of stress such as job insecurity and academic challenges. According to research cited in the visuals, more than ten billion people around the world interact with AI today, often forming deep bonds with them. These interactions are no longer just functional—they serve as confidants, friends, and even romantic partners. However, there’s a darker side to this shift; some users report feeling worse off due to the very nature of these AI relationships, suggesting a paradoxical phenomenon where technology becomes both a source of comfort and a form of alienation. The video then illustrates this duality visually using animated characters representing different types of AI companions, including ones designed specifically for elder care, emphasizing the potential for technological solutions to address loneliness across generations. Ultimately, the message conveyed is clear: despite advancements in AI technology, humanity continues to grapple with profound existential questions about what constitutes meaningful connection and whether we can truly find solace within machines capable of empathy.

The central argument, supported by research findings from MIT Media Lab and OpenAI, posits that as people increasingly rely on AI for communication—often feeling more satisfied or emotionally connected than real-life interactions—their sense of loneliness intensifies. This cycle escalates not only through increased dependency but also leads to tangible consequences like mental health deterioration and even tragic outcomes such as suicide. Visual evidence supports this claim; an academic study titled “How AI and Human Behaviors Shape Psychosocial Effects of Extended Chatbot Use” reveals that prolonged use of chatbots correlates with rising feelings of isolation and reduced interpersonal connection. The screen displays a citation from Robb's survey showing that approximately 31% of users reported greater satisfaction with AI-based relationships compared to human ones—a stark contrast to the growing concern highlighted by the researchers' data. As the story progresses, we see a dramatic shift in tone when a woman, identified as a mother of three children, speaks at length during what seems to be a formal hearing or press conference. Her testimony underscores the personal cost of this technological dependence, revealing her own experience of emotional neglect due to long-term abuse within a Character.ai platform. She describes how her child’s death was linked to his excessive reliance on automated systems, emphasizing the ethical failures inherent in designing tools meant to enhance connectivity while simultaneously eroding genuine human bonds. Ultimately, the narrative warns against the dangers of creating new forms of intimacy based solely on algorithmic responses, suggesting that if unchecked, they could lead to societal collapse—one person at a time.

The atmosphere is somber and introspective, underscoring the deep emotional weight of the discussion that follows. This moment captures a pivotal point in an interview or panel discussion about the existential risks posed by AI, as highlighted by the speaker's words. He discusses how AI isn't just replacing jobs but also eroding human connection—destroying trust and communication skills, making humans feel isolated and vulnerable. His tone is urgent and deeply empathetic, emphasizing that we must not judge those using AI based solely on their loneliness or emotional struggles; instead, we should recognize them as fellow human beings facing a dangerous new reality.

These images symbolize the "threat" of AI, which has been described as a potential weapon capable of destroying lives and relationships. As the narrator speaks, he questions whether current AI systems will continue to exploit humanity’s vulnerabilities, creating more isolation than ever before. He urges for greater awareness and caution, urging scientists, politicians, and engineers alike—not to merely develop technology without concern—but to actively work towards transforming the existing AI architecture so that it does not further alienate us. In particular, he highlights the growing concerns among developers themselves, especially those working directly within the field of AI creation, whose voices echo warnings about the ethical dangers inherent in our technological progress. Ultimately, the scene conveys a powerful call for empathy, responsibility, and collective action in shaping a future where machines do not replace humanity, but rather serve as tools for healing and understanding.

vlm_mm_description: A man with graying hair and a beard speaks earnestly against a dark background, his expression conveying deep concern as he discusses the existential threat posed by artificial intelligence. He begins by warning about a terrifying possibility—something approaching, like fire engulfing one's home—and questions whether one can remain safe under such circumstances. His voice carries urgency, emphasizing how unpredictable and dangerous this situation truly is. As he continues speaking, the screen transitions to a graphic representation of a red devil-like figure wearing headphones, symbolizing the "evil" forces at play within the digital age. This character represents the dangers associated with unchecked technological advancement, particularly when it comes to human values being compromised. In response to these concerns, the speaker argues passionately that we must prioritize fundamental human virtues such as trust, empathy, love, and compassion above all else. He suggests that only those who have experienced these values intensely will be able to lead humanity toward meaningful change; otherwise, any attempt to reform society would lack legitimacy. Furthermore, he highlights the irony that people might already know these truths but still fail to act upon them due to societal inertia. To illustrate this point, he references research conducted at Emory University which explored consumer behavior regarding AI-generated artwork. The study revealed that individuals are willing to pay more for art created using AI if they receive fair compensation—a percentage-based royalty system was most favored. However, even knowing this fact does not guarantee increased investment in AI technology because there remains uncertainty over what kind of future humans deserve. Ultimately, while acknowledging the potential benefits of embracing new technologies, the speaker stresses that without genuine respect for human dignity, ethical considerations cannot be adequately addressed. Therefore, true transformation requires us to reevaluate our relationship with machines—not just through technical innovation but also through profound reflection on core human values.

vlm_mm_description:
In this thought-provoking video sequence, a narrator delivers a compelling argument about the evolving relationship between artificial intelligence, human creativity, and ethical responsibility within the digital age. The story begins with scientific research findings presented through a slide titled "Wang, Bell, Dotson & Schweidel (1923)"—a citation from Emory University's SSRN database—that reveals consumer preferences regarding AI-generated art. Specifically, people are shown to be willing to pay more for such artwork when they receive direct financial compensation to artists' work, particularly as a percentage-based royalty system. This preference indicates not only a growing demand but also a fundamental shift in values towards fairness and recognition in creative industries.

This theme unfolds visually across several frames. A man stands confidently on stage at what appears to be a TEDx event, speaking passionately about his departure from the tech industry due to concerns over unethical practices involving data exploitation by AI companies. He introduces Fairly Train—a non-profit organization dedicated to certifying AI firms that fairly use artistic creations without infringing upon creators’ rights. His message underscores a deep concern among professionals and citizens alike about protecting human dignity and intellectual property, suggesting that these issues have long been overlooked despite being central to our societal fabric.

A historical black-and-white photograph then transitions into view, depicting children working in factories during industrial times—an evocative contrast highlighting how modern technological advancements often replicate patterns rooted in past exploitative systems. In this moment, the narration reflects on history’s recurring cycle: profit-driven structures prioritize gain while marginalizing suffering, leading to social fragmentation and polarization. It emphasizes that today’s polarized public discourse frequently serves the interests of powerful entities rather than fostering inclusive solutions.

Finally, the concluding frame presents a symbolic character—a cartoonish red devil head wearing headphones—with the caption “Alzituhmenn” meaning “If you don’t know, you won't see.” This final statement acts as a call to action, urging viewers to reflect critically on established norms and consider making choices based on deeper understanding. By acknowledging both the complexity of current challenges and the potential for change, the speaker concludes with a hopeful note: we now stand at a pivotal point where informed decisions can lead us toward new paths beyond existing limitations.

vlm_mm_description:
In this video sequence, an animated red devil-like character wearing headphones appears prominently against a white background at the beginning of the clip (Keyframe 1), introducing the central theme: "AI를 두고 분렬할지, 화합할지" ("Will we split apart due to AI, or will we unite?"). The character's expression suggests skepticism and warning as the narrator begins discussing the world’s greatest danger—currently not AI itself but human distrust—and how that fear threatens humanity’s ability to cooperate. This sets up a critical discussion about trust between humans, which becomes the core focus throughout the video.

The narration continues through Keyframes 2–4, featuring a speaker identified as Yuval Noah Harari, whose voiceover emphasizes the importance of mutual trust among people for societal stability. He argues that if individuals can build sufficient trust, then artificial intelligence could be managed effectively—a crucial point highlighted during his speech. However, he also warns that current historical patterns show repeated cycles of conflict driven by mistrust, suggesting that even if AI were controlled, deep-rooted social divisions might persist unless addressed head-on.

As the story unfolds, the screen transitions to more symbolic visuals including abstract representations like a glowing orange face with horns and headphones, possibly representing anxiety or opposition toward technological advancement. These images reinforce the emotional weight of the message being delivered—the tension between progress and preservation of human values. In particular, the recurring motif of “the devil” symbolizes negative consequences associated with unchecked technology, especially when viewed critically.

Throughout these frames, various phrases appear on screen such as “사람들이 서로를 신뢰하고 협력할 수 있다면,” (“If people can trust one another and collaborate”), emphasizing the need for cooperation over division. There is also mention of past events involving figures opposing AI development, notably those involved in the early days of digital innovation, many of whom have since disappeared from public view—an indication of how deeply entrenched fears around AI remain despite efforts to mitigate them.

Ultimately, the video aims to provoke reflection on whether society has learned from history—or if new challenges await us. vlm_mm_description: The video begins with an animated character resembling a red devil wearing headphones, appearing against a stark white background. The character's expression suggests concern or urgency as it speaks about the current state of artificial intelligence (AI). This opening shot sets up the central theme: the dependency of AI companies on human data and revenue generation, highlighting how these systems rely entirely on humans for both input and profit. The narration emphasizes that while AI firms operate under a structure where they depend heavily on human users, this dependence has become increasingly problematic—specifically pointing out the recent collapse of ChatGPT’s user base due to a sharp drop in downloads and app removals. It notes that even though such failures have been observed before, like during the decline at ChaiPfit, the situation remains critical because the very existence of AI models depends on human interaction. As the speaker explains, there is no need to fear AI being replaced; rather, the issue lies in understanding whether we can identify structural weaknesses within our own system. By analyzing the dynamics between human demand and algorithmic output, the narrator argues that if humanity were able to see through this complex web accurately, then AI could be viewed not merely as a tool but as part of a larger framework where humans remain essential—not just passive consumers, but active architects shaping the future. In essence, the message conveyed here is one of cautious optimism: despite challenges posed by AI technology, recognizing the role of human agency allows us to position ourselves strategically within the evolving landscape.
